    # Installation and Configuration\r\n
    > You can find the full documentation of this project step by step in this README note.\r\n
    - I have buit this system for personal use. I do not recommend using it for work-related tasks. Unless YOU teste and confirm that it works as expected, do not use it for work-related tasks.\r\n
    \r\n
    **Installing Laravel**\r\n
    \r\n
    - - First, you need to install PHP on your system. You can download it from the official website.\r\n
    \r\n
    - Next, you need to install Composer. You can download it from the official website.\r\n
    \r\n
    - Once you have installed PHP and Composer, you can install Laravel by running the following command in your terminal:\r\n
    \r\n
    - Then you can clone the Laravel repository by running the following command:\r\n
    ```url\r\n
    \thttps://github.com/Saboor-Hamedi/sms_laravel.git\r\n
    ```\r\n
     - After cloning the repository, you need to install npm and update everything by running the following commands:\r\n
    ### Install spatie\r\n
     - Consult the Prerequisites page for important considerations regarding\r\n
       your User models! This package publishes a config/permission.php\r\n
       file. If you already have a file by that name, you must rename or\r\n
       remove it. You can install the package via composer:\r\n
       \r\n
     -  ` composer require spatie/laravel-permission`\r\n
     -  `npm install && npm update`\r\n
     -  `composer dump-autoload`\r\n
     -  `composer update`\r\n
     - Run migrations and seeders:\r\n
    `php artisan migrate:fresh --seed`\r\n
     - Finally, you can run the server by running the following command:\r\n
    \r\n
    `php artisan serve`
    """
